Dropped Grades: Why the Lowest Percentage May Not Be Removed

Understand dropped-grade policies for equal-weight scores and pooled points, with an example where removing the lowest percentage is not the best group result.

By GradeTargetCalc · Published 2 November 2026 · 5 min read

In this guide
The word lowest does not define the whole ruleIdentify the eligible set firstEqual-weight percentages are the simpler caseA pooled-points example changes the decisionRead what the gradebook actually optimizesApply the category weight after the dropExpect a provisional exclusion to changeA short checklist for an unexplained resultFAQsSources
01

The word lowest does not define the whole rule

A syllabus may say that one quiz grade is dropped, but that phrase alone does not identify every detail of the calculation. Which assignments are eligible? Are scores averaged as equal percentages or pooled as raw points? Does the system remove the smallest percentage or the assignment whose removal produces the best group result?

Those questions matter when assessments have different point totals. A short weak quiz and a large moderately weak exam can affect the pooled group differently. Reconstruct the stated rule before treating a calculator result as an explanation of what the gradebook must display.

02

Identify the eligible set first

List each assessment’s earned points, possible points and whether it can be dropped. Check for a minimum number of completed tasks, protected assessments and rules about missing work. An assignment marked “never drop” must remain even when its removal would raise the mathematical average.

Only remove a zero if the policy allows that particular assessment to be excluded. A blank for ungraded work is different from an awarded zero, and a compulsory-submission condition may still apply. Do not change the source record while experimenting; keep the original scores beside each hypothetical scenario.

03

Equal-weight percentages are the simpler case

For four equally important quiz percentages of 60, 80, 90 and 100, the original mean is 330 ÷ 4 = 82.5%. Dropping the lowest eligible percentage leaves 80, 90 and 100, which average 270 ÷ 3 = 90%. Both the sum and the count change.

The Drop Lowest Grade Calculator uses this equal-weight percentage model. It does not examine raw assignment point totals or decide which assessments are policy-eligible. Entering unequal-point assignments as percentages silently changes their importance unless the instructor actually assigns them equal weight.

04

A pooled-points example changes the decision

Consider three assessments scored 6/10, 70/100 and 90/100. Their percentages are 60%, 70% and 90%. The pooled group score is (6 + 70 + 90) ÷ (10 + 100 + 100) × 100 = 79.05%. Each available point has equal importance in this system.

Removing the lowest percentage, 6/10, leaves 160/200 = 80%. Removing 70/100 instead leaves 96/110 = 87.27%. Removing 90/100 leaves 76/110 = 69.09%. Therefore the best pooled result comes from removing the 70% assessment, even though 60% is the smallest percentage in the original list.

05

Read what the gradebook actually optimizes

Instructure’s official Canvas documentation explains that its assignment-group drop rule can select the removal that most improves the group total. It is therefore unsafe to assume that every gradebook’s “lowest score” label refers only to sorting displayed percentages. Inspect the actual rule and point structure.

That behavior does not establish a universal policy across all platforms or courses. Your instructor’s syllabus and configured group rules still determine the eligible calculations. When the displayed exclusion surprises you, compare the retained earned-and-possible totals before concluding that the software has made an arithmetic error.

06

Apply the category weight after the drop

Suppose the example group contributes 20% of the course. A retained group score of 87.27% contributes approximately 17.45 course percentage points. A retained score of 80% contributes sixteen points. The difference at course level is smaller than the difference between the group percentages because the category supplies only one fifth of the course.

Keep unrounded fractions for your manual check where possible. For the better pooled outcome, 96 ÷ 110 × 0.20 × 100 = 17.4545… course points. Do not multiply each retained assignment separately by the full 20% category weight; that would apply the category’s importance more than once.

07

Expect a provisional exclusion to change

When new grades arrive, the best removal may change because both the group’s score distribution and available point total change. An assessment currently shown as dropped is not necessarily permanently excluded from the final record. Check whether the course applies drops continuously or only once all required work has been marked.

A plan based on an expected future drop should therefore be labeled provisional. Recalculate after each new assessment and verify that the required number of eligible scores exists. Do not assume the exclusion can be used a second time in another category or that it removes an independent attendance or submission condition.

08

A short checklist for an unexplained result

Check the eligible assignments, retained numerator, retained denominator, category weight and any protected scores. Then calculate the plausible removal alternatives. If one matches the gradebook, describe that mathematical rule clearly when asking the instructor for confirmation.

Use the Grade Percentage Calculator for each retained pooled total, the Drop Lowest Grade Calculator for genuinely equal-weight percentages and the Weighted Grade Calculator for combining the resulting category with others. Choosing the correct model is more important than choosing the model that gives the highest number.

Quick answers

Frequently asked questions

Can the equal-percentage calculator reproduce every Canvas drop?

No. It averages equal-weight percentages. Unequal possible points and eligibility rules require a separate retained-points calculation.

Does a dropped score disappear from my academic record?

This guide concerns its exclusion from a calculation. Display, transcript and submission treatment depend on institutional and course rules.

Why did the dropped assignment change after another quiz?

A new score can change which eligible removal produces the best group result. Check how and when the configured rule is applied.
